name: visualization
description: Draw anything a reader has to look at to understand — 39 editorial diagram types (architecture, flowchart, sequence, state, ER, timeline, swimlane, quadrant, radar, polar, loop, nested, tree, org chart, layer stack, Venn, pyramid, treemap, Sankey, fishbone, Wardley map, kanban, journey, deployment, dependency, UML class, story map, DB schema and more) and the quantitative chart forms (bar, line, area, scatter, bubble, beeswarm, dumbbell, slopegraph, bump, ridgeline, heatmap, stat tile, meter, hero figure) as one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG. The merge is the point: a diagram system that was strong on layout grammar had a five-colour series palette chosen by eye, and it fails a perceptual gate in both light and dark — five of five slots below the chroma floor, worst normal-vision ΔE 10.3 against a floor of 15, which is five greys with a tint. This version routes the form from the data's job before colour, snaps a brand's own hue families to a passing palette by re-stepping and re-ordering them, and holds charts to zero-baseline, one-scale, area-by-area and disclosed-gap honesty rules the diagram side never needed. It also ships the gates: the predecessor cited twenty verifier scripts that existed only in its repository, so the installed agent doing the drawing could cite a check it could not run — twelve now ship inside the skill, run from the install against the file just written, and exit non-zero. Redraws .drawio or Mermaid sources at a chosen size and detail, onboards brand tokens from a website, and adds semantic patterns, callouts, accessible motion or hand-drawn styling. Successor to diagram-design by Cathryn Lavery, whose 39 layout grammars, six connector rules and import pipeline it keeps intact.
